sanskrit: tataḥ prāguttarāṃ gatvā rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha viśvāmitraṃ puraskṛtya yajñavāṭam upāgamat
english: Then Rāma, together with Saumitri [Lakṣmaṇa], having gone toward the northeast and placing Viśvāmitra at their head, came to the sacrificial enclosure.

sanskrit: rāmas tu muniśārdūlam uvāca sahalakṣmaṇaḥ sādhvī yajñasamṛddhir hi janakasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Rāma, together with Lakṣmaṇa, said to that tiger among sages: 'Indeed the sacrificial prosperity of the great-souled Janaka is remarkable.'

sanskrit: bahūnīha sahasrāṇi nānādeśanivāsinām brāhmaṇānāṃ mahābhāga vedādhyayanaśālinām
english: 'Here there are many thousands of brāhmaṇas, O greatly fortunate one, dwelling from various regions, distinguished by their study of the Vedas.'

sanskrit: ṛṣivāṭāś ca dṛśyante śakaṭīśatasaṃkulāḥ deśo vidhīyatāṃ brahman yatra vatsyāmahe vayam
english: 'And the hermitages of seers are visible, thronged with hundreds of carts. O brāhmaṇa, kindly designate a place where we may lodge.'

sanskrit: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ niveśam akarod deśe vivikte salilāyute
english: Hearing Rāma's words, the great sage Viśvāmitra arranged their lodging in a secluded spot well supplied with water.

sanskrit: viśvāmitraṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ śrutvā sa nṛpatis tadā śatānandaṃ puraskṛtya purohitam aninditam
english: When the king heard of Viśvāmitra, that foremost among sages, he then came forward, placing at his head Śatānanda, his blameless royal chaplain.

sanskrit: ṛtvijo 'pi mahātmānas tv arghyam ādāya satvaram viśvāmitrāya dharmeṇa dadur mantrapuraskṛtam
english: The great-souled officiating priests too, swiftly taking the arghya [honorific offering of water], presented it to Viśvāmitra with due rite, accompanied by Vedic mantras.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu tāṃ pūjāṃ janakasya mahātmanaḥ papraccha kuśalaṃ rājño yajñasya ca nirāmayam
english: Having received that honor from the great-souled Janaka, [Viśvāmitra] enquired after the king's welfare and the unimpeded progress of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: sa tāṃś cāpi munīn pṛṣṭvā sopādhyāya purodhasaḥ yathānyāyaṃ tataḥ sarvaiḥ samāgacchat prahṛṣṭavān
english: He, having inquired after the welfare of those sages together with the preceptors and priests, then met with all of them according to proper custom, filled with delight.

sanskrit: atha rājā muniśreṣṭhaṃ kṛtāñjalir abhāṣata āsane bhagavān āstāṃ sahaibhir munisattamaiḥ
english: Then the king, with joined palms, addressed that foremost sage: 'Let the Blessed One be seated, along with these eminent sages.'

sanskrit: janakasya vacaḥ śrutvā niṣasāda mahāmuniḥ purodhā ṛtvijaś caiva rājā ca saha mantribhiḥ
english: Hearing Janaka's words, the great sage sat down, as did the chaplain, the officiating priests, and the king together with his ministers.

sanskrit: āsaneṣu yathānyāyam upaviṣṭān samantataḥ dṛṣṭvā sa nṛpatis tatra viśvāmitram athābravīt
english: Seeing them seated all around in their proper places, the king there then spoke to Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: adya yajñasamṛddhir me saphalā daivataiḥ kṛtā adya yajñaphalaṃ prāptaṃ bhagavaddarśanān mayā
english: 'Today the prosperity of my sacrifice has been made fruitful by the gods; today I have attained the fruit of the sacrifice by virtue of your blessed presence.'

sanskrit: dhanyo 'smy anugṛhīto 'smi yasya me munipuṃgava yajñopasadanaṃ brahman prāpto 'si munibhiḥ saha
english: 'I am blessed, I am favored, O bull among sages, in that you, O brāhmaṇa, have come to my sacrifice together with the sages.'

sanskrit: dvādaśāhaṃ tu brahmarṣe śeṣam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ tato bhāgārthino devān draṣṭum arhasi kauśika
english: 'The wise declare that twelve days remain, O brahmarṣi; thereafter, O Kauśika, you shall behold the gods who come to receive their share [of the offerings].'

sanskrit: ity uktvā muniśārdūlaṃ prahṛṣṭavadanas tadā punas taṃ paripapraccha prāñjaliḥ prayato nṛpaḥ
english: Having spoken thus to that tiger among sages, the king, with joyful countenance and joined palms, reverently questioned him again.

sanskrit: imau kumārau bhadraṃ te devatulyaparākramau gajasiṃhagatī vīrau śārdūlavṛṣabhopamau
english: 'Be it well with you — these two princes, whose valor equals the gods', heroes who move with the gait of elephant and lion, comparable to a tiger and a bull —'

sanskrit: padmapatraviśālākṣau khaḍgatūṇīdhanurdharau aśvināv iva rūpeṇa samupasthitayauvanau
english: '— with eyes wide as lotus petals, bearing sword, quiver, and bow, like the two Aśvins in beauty, arrived at the fullness of youth —'

sanskrit: yadṛcchayaiva gāṃ prāptau devalokād ivāmarau kathaṃ padbhyām iha prāptau kimarthaṃ kasya vā mune
english: '— having reached the earth as if by chance, like immortals from the world of gods — how have they arrived here on foot, O sage, and for what purpose, and whose [sons] are they?'

sanskrit: varāyudhadharau vīrau kasya putrau mahāmune bhūṣayantāv imaṃ deśaṃ candrasūryāv ivāmbaram
english: 'Bearing excellent weapons, valiant heroes — whose sons are they, O great sage? They adorn this region as the moon and sun adorn the sky.'

sanskrit: parasparasya sadṛśau pramāṇeṅgitaceṣṭitaiḥ kākapakṣadharau vīrau śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: 'Resembling each other in stature, bearing, and conduct, these two heroes wearing their hair in the kakapakṣa style — I desire to learn the truth about them.'

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā janakasya mahātmanaḥ nyavedayan mahātmānau putrau daśarathasya tau
english: Hearing those words of the great-souled Janaka, the two great-souled ones announced themselves as the sons of Daśaratha.

sanskrit: siddhāśramanivāsaṃ ca rākṣasānāṃ vadhaṃ tathā tac cāgamanam avyagraṃ viśālāyāś ca darśanam
english: [Viśvāmitra narrated] their dwelling at Siddhāśrama, the slaying of the rākṣasas, their unhindered journey hither, and the sight of Viśālā.

sanskrit: ahalyādarśanaṃ caiva gautamena samāgamam mahādhanuṣi jijñāsāṃ kartum āgamanaṃ tathā
english: And the beholding of Ahalyā, the meeting with Gautama, and their arrival here in order to see the great bow.

sanskrit: etat sarvaṃ mahātejā janakāya mahātmane nivedya virarāmātha viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
english: Having reported all this to the great-souled Janaka, the great sage Viśvāmitra of mighty splendor then fell silent.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ hṛṣṭaromā mahātejāḥ śatānando mahātapāḥ
english: Hearing those words of the wise Viśvāmitra, Śatānanda of great splendor and mighty austerities had the hair on his body stand erect with joy.

sanskrit: gautamasya suto jyeṣṭhas tapasā dyotitaprabhaḥ rāmasaṃdarśanād eva paraṃ vismayam āgataḥ
english: The eldest son of Gautama, whose luster blazed forth through his austerities, was overcome with the highest wonder at the very sight of Rāma.

sanskrit: sa tau niṣaṇṇau saṃprekṣya sukhāsīnau nṛpātmajau śatānando muniśreṣṭhaṃ viśvāmitram athābravīt
english: Gazing at those two princes seated at ease, Śatānanda then spoke to Viśvāmitra, that foremost among sages.

sanskrit: api te muniśārdūla mama mātā yaśasvinī darśitā rājaputrāya tapo dīrgham upāgatā
english: 'O tiger among sages, was my illustrious mother, who had practised long austerities, shown to the prince?'

sanskrit: api rāme mahātejo mama mātā yaśasvinī vanyair upāharat pūjāṃ pūjārhe sarvadehinām
english: 'O you of great splendor, did my illustrious mother offer worship to Rāma with forest [gifts], to him who is worthy of worship by all embodied beings?'

sanskrit: api rāmāya kathitaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ purātanam mama mātur mahātejo devena duranuṣṭhitam
english: 'O you of great splendor, was the ancient event relating to my mother, that which the god [Indra] caused to be carried out wrongfully, narrated to Rāma?'

sanskrit: api kauśika bhadraṃ te guruṇā mama saṃgatā mātā mama muniśreṣṭha rāmasaṃdarśanād itaḥ
english: 'O Kauśika, may it be well with you — was my mother reunited with my guru [Gautama] here, after the sight of Rāma, O foremost among sages?'

sanskrit: api me guruṇā rāmaḥ pūjitaḥ kuśikātmaja ihāgato mahātejāḥ pūjāṃ prāpya mahātmanaḥ
english: 'O son of Kuśika, was Rāma of great splendor honored by my guru, having come here and received worship from that great soul?'

sanskrit: api śāntena manasā gurur me kuśikātmaja ihāgatena rāmeṇa prayatenābhivāditaḥ
english: 'O son of Kuśika, was my guru, with tranquil mind, reverently saluted by Rāma who had come here with pure devotion?'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ pratyuvāca śatānandaṃ vākyajño vākyakovidam
english: Hearing his words, the great sage Viśvāmitra, skilled in speech, replied to Śatānanda, who was himself versed in eloquent speech.

sanskrit: nātikrāntaṃ muniśreṣṭha yat kartavyaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā saṃgatā muninā patnī bhārgaveṇeva reṇukā
english: 'O foremost among sages, nothing beyond what was proper has been transgressed by me; the wife [Ahalyā] has been reunited with the sage [Gautama], even as Reṇukā [was reunited] with Bhārgava [Jamadagni].'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ śatānando mahātejā rāmaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing those words of the wise Viśvāmitra, the great-splendored Śatānanda addressed Rāma with these words.

sanskrit: svāgataṃ te naraśreṣṭha diṣṭyā prāpto 'si rāghava viśvāmitraṃ puraskṛtya maharṣim aparājitam
english: 'Welcome to you, O foremost among men; by good fortune have you arrived, O Rāghava, placing at your head the unconquered great sage Viśvāmitra.'

sanskrit: acintyakarmā tapasā brahmarṣir amitaprabhaḥ viśvāmitro mahātejā vetsy enaṃ paramāṃ gatim
english: 'Viśvāmitra of mighty splendor, a brahmarṣi of inconceivable deeds and boundless radiance through his austerities — know him to be the highest refuge.'

sanskrit: nāsti dhanyataro rāma tvatto 'nyo bhuvi kaś cana goptā kuśikaputras te yena taptaṃ mahat tapaḥ
english: 'There is none more blessed on earth than you, O Rāma; the son of Kuśika is your guardian, he who has practised great austerity.'

sanskrit: śrūyatāṃ cābhidāsyāmi kauśikasya mahātmanaḥ yathābalaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: 'And do listen — I shall recount the history of the great-souled Kauśika as best I can; hear it from me as I narrate it in full.'

sanskrit: rājābhūd eṣa dharmātmā dīrgha kālam ariṃdamaḥ dharmajñaḥ kṛtavidyaś ca prajānāṃ ca hite rataḥ
english: 'This one [Viśvāmitra] was a king for a long time, a subduer of enemies, righteous in soul, knowing dharma, accomplished in learning, and devoted to the welfare of his subjects.'

sanskrit: prajāpatisutas tv āsīt kuśo nāma mahīpatiḥ kuśasya putro balavān kuśanābhaḥ sudhārmikaḥ
english: 'There was a lord of the earth, son of Prajāpati, named Kuśa; Kuśa's son was the powerful and highly righteous Kuśanābha.'

sanskrit: kuśanābhasutas tv āsīd gādhir ity eva viśrutaḥ gādheḥ putro mahātejā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
english: 'Kuśanābha's son was celebrated by the name Gādhi; Gādhi's son is the mighty and splendorous great sage Viśvāmitra.'

sanskrit: viśvamitro mahātejāḥ pālayām āsa medinīm bahuvarṣasahasrāṇi rājā rājyam akārayat
english: 'The mighty Viśvāmitra governed the earth; as king he ruled the kingdom for many thousands of years.'

sanskrit: kadā cit tu mahātejā yojayitvā varūthinīm akṣauhiṇīparivṛtaḥ paricakrāma medinīm
english: 'At a certain time the mighty one, having marshaled his army, surrounded by an akṣauhiṇī [a full military division], roamed the earth.'

sanskrit: nagarāṇi ca rāṣṭrāṇi saritaś ca tathā girīn āśramān kramaśo rājā vicarann ājagāmaha
english: 'Wandering through cities, kingdoms, rivers, mountains, and hermitages in succession, the king came [at last] —'

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhasyāśramapadaṃ nānāpuṣpaphaladrumam nānāmṛgagaṇākīrṇaṃ siddhacāraṇasevitam
english: '— to the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha, adorned with trees bearing various flowers and fruits, filled with many herds of deer, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.'

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvaiḥ kiṃnarair upaśobhitam praśāntahariṇākīrṇaṃ dvijasaṃghaniṣevitam
english: 'Beautified by gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, and Kiṃnaras; filled with tranquil deer; frequented by throngs of twice-born ones.'

sanskrit: brahmarṣigaṇasaṃkīrṇaṃ devarṣigaṇasevitam tapaścaraṇasaṃsiddhair agnikalpair mahātmabhiḥ
english: 'Crowded with hosts of brahmarṣis, served by bands of divine sages, and by great souls perfected through the practice of austerities, who were like fires [in their splendor].'

sanskrit: satataṃ saṃkulaṃ śrīmad brahmakalpair mahātmabhiḥ abbhakṣair vāyubhakṣaiś ca śīrṇaparṇāśanais tathā
english: 'Ever thronged with resplendent great souls equal to Brahmā — those who subsist on water, those who subsist on air, and those who eat only fallen leaves.'

sanskrit: phalamūlāśanair dāntair jitaroṣair jitendriyaiḥ ṛṣibhir vālakhilyaiś ca japahomaparāyaṇaiḥ
english: '[And by seers] who subsist on fruit and roots, who are self-restrained, who have conquered anger, who have conquered the senses, and by the Vālakhilya sages devoted to japa and homa.'

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhasyāśramapadaṃ brahmalokam ivāparam dadarśa jayatāṃ śreṣṭha viśvāmitro mahābalaḥ
english: 'Vasiṣṭha's hermitage, like another realm of Brahmā — this the mighty Viśvāmitra, foremost among the victorious, beheld.'

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā paramaprīto viśvāmitro mahābalaḥ praṇato vinayād vīro vasiṣṭhaṃ japatāṃ varam
english: Beholding it, the mighty Viśvāmitra was exceedingly pleased; the hero, bowing with humility, [approached] Vasiṣṭha, the best among those who recite [the Vedas].

sanskrit: svāgataṃ tava cety ukto vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā āsanaṃ cāsya bhagavān vasiṣṭho vyādideśa ha
english: Addressed with 'welcome' by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, the blessed Vasiṣṭha also indicated a seat for him.

sanskrit: upaviṣṭāya ca tadā viśvāmitrāya dhīmate yathānyāyaṃ munivaraḥ phalamūlam upāharat
english: And when the wise Viśvāmitra had taken his seat, that foremost sage offered him fruits and roots in accordance with proper custom.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tāṃ pūjāṃ vasiṣṭhād rājasattamaḥ tapo'gnihotraśiṣyeṣu kuśalaṃ paryapṛcchata
english: Having accepted that honor from Vasiṣṭha, the foremost among kings [Viśvāmitra] enquired after the welfare of [his] pupils in austerities, the agnihotra, and [the sacred fires].

sanskrit: viśvāmitro mahātejā vanaspatigaṇe tathā sarvatra kuśalaṃ cāha vasiṣṭho rājasattamam
english: The greatly splendorous Viśvāmitra likewise [enquired] about the trees of the forest; and Vasiṣṭha declared to that foremost among kings that all was well in every respect.

sanskrit: sukhopaviṣṭaṃ rājānaṃ viśvāmitraṃ mahātapāḥ papraccha japatāṃ śreṣṭho vasiṣṭho brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha, son of Brahmā, the foremost among those who recite [the Vedas] and of mighty austerities, then questioned the king Viśvāmitra, who was seated comfortably.

sanskrit: kaccit te kuśalaṃ rājan kaccid dharmeṇa rañjayan prajāḥ pālayase rājan rājavṛttena dhārmika
english: 'Is all well with you, O king? Do you, O righteous king, cherish and protect your subjects with righteousness and with the conduct befitting a king?'

sanskrit: kaccit te subhṛtā bhṛtyāḥ kaccit tiṣṭhanti śāsane kaccit te vijitāḥ sarve ripavo ripusūdana
english: 'Are your servants well provided for? Do they abide by your commands? Have all your enemies been subdued, O slayer of foes?'

sanskrit: kaccid bale ca kośe ca mitreṣu ca paraṃtapa kuśalaṃ te naravyāghra putrapautre tathānagha
english: 'Is all well with your army, treasury, and allies, O scorcher of enemies? Is all well with your sons and grandsons, O tiger among men, O blameless one?'

sanskrit: sarvatra kuśalaṃ rājā vasiṣṭhaṃ pratyudāharat viśvāmitro mahātejā vasiṣṭhaṃ vinayānvitaḥ
english: The king Viśvāmitra of great splendor, filled with humility, declared to Vasiṣṭha that all was well in every respect.

sanskrit: kṛtvobhau suciraṃ kālaṃ dharmiṣṭhau tāḥ kathāḥ śubhāḥ mudā paramayā yuktau prīyetāṃ tau parasparam
english: Both of them, most righteous in conduct, having exchanged those auspicious pleasantries for a long time, filled with the highest joy, delighted in each other's company.

sanskrit: tato vasiṣṭho bhagavān kathānte raghunandana viśvāmitram idaṃ vākyam uvāca prahasann iva
english: Then at the end of their conversation, O delight of the Raghu line, the blessed Vasiṣṭha spoke this word to Viśvāmitra with a smile.

sanskrit: ātithyaṃ kartum icchāmi balasyāsya mahābala tava caivāprameyasya yathārhaṃ saṃpratīccha me
english: 'I wish to offer hospitality, O mighty one, to this army of yours and to you yourself, who are beyond measure; please accept what is fitting from me.'

sanskrit: satkriyāṃ tu bhavān etāṃ pratīcchatu mayodyatām rājaṃs tvam atithiśreṣṭhaḥ pūjanīyaḥ prayatnataḥ
english: 'Let Your Honor accept this honor prepared by me; O king, you are the most excellent of guests and are worthy of being honored with care.'

sanskrit: evam ukto vasiṣṭhena viśvāmitro mahāmatiḥ kṛtam ity abravīd rājā pūjāvākyena me tvayā
english: Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, the great-minded Viśvāmitra, king, said: 'It has been done — you have honored me with words of respect.'

sanskrit: phalamūlena bhagavan vidyate yat tavāśrame pādyenācamanīyena bhagavaddarśanena ca
english: 'With whatever fruit and roots there are in your hermitage, O blessed one, and with water for the feet and for sipping, and with the sight of your blessed self —'

sanskrit: sarvathā ca mahāprājña pūjārheṇa supūjitaḥ gamiṣyāmi namas te 'stu maitreṇekṣasva cakṣuṣā
english: '— in every way, O greatly wise one, honored by one worthy of honor, I shall depart. Let my obeisance be unto you; look upon me with a friendly eye.'

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvantaṃ rājānaṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ punar eva hi nyamantrayata dharmātmā punaḥ punar udāradhīḥ
english: As the king spoke thus, Vasiṣṭha, righteous in soul and noble in mind, pressed his invitation upon him again and again.

sanskrit: bāḍham ity eva gādheyo vasiṣṭhaṃ pratyuvāca ha yathā priyaṃ bhagavatas tathāstu munisattama
english: The son of Gādhi [Viśvāmitra] replied to Vasiṣṭha simply: 'So be it — let it be as the Blessed One desires, O foremost among sages.'

sanskrit: evam ukto mahātejā vasiṣṭho japatāṃ varaḥ ājuhāva tataḥ prītaḥ kalmāṣīṃ dhūtakalmaṣaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the great-splendored Vasiṣṭha, best among those who recite [the Vedas], free from all impurity, then joyfully summoned Kalmāṣī [Śabalā, the speckled cow].

sanskrit: ehy ehi śabale kṣipraṃ śṛṇu cāpi vaco mama sabalasyāsya rājarṣeḥ kartuṃ vyavasito 'smy aham bhojanena mahārheṇa satkāraṃ saṃvidhatsva me
english: 'Come, come quickly, O Śabalā, and hear my words too; I am resolved to honor this royal sage together with his army — prepare for me a most worthy feast.'

sanskrit: yasya yasya yathākāmaṃ ṣaḍraseṣv abhipūjitam tat sarvaṃ kāmadhug divye abhivarṣakṛte mama
english: 'Whatever and whichever [food], as desired, honored in the six flavors — all of that, O divine wish-granting cow, rain down for me [now].'

sanskrit: rasenānnena pānena lehyacoṣyeṇa saṃyutam annānāṃ nicayaṃ sarvaṃ sṛjasva śabale tvara
english: 'Create for me, O Śabalā, the complete store of foods combined with savory dishes, drink, lickables, and suckables — make haste!'
